caveats: Needs two concurrent POST requests to login_totp, each with a session past the password stage for the same user, submitting the same valid code within its ~90s window (e.g. attacker-controlled sessions racing a stolen code).
Needs concurrently served requests (threads, processes or workers) with separate DB connections; deployment model is UNCONFIRMED.

Needs a DB where the SELECT-then-UPDATE interleaving is possible (e.g. Postgres read-committed, the production engine per hc/settings.py:125-141); under the default dev sqlite3 backend concurrent writes serialize and the window narrows.
Relies on Django get_or_create retry-on-IntegrityError semantics and DB unique-constraint enforcement, both outside this tree.
subclaims.reason: Two concurrent POSTs to hc/accounts/views.py:881 each pass TOTP validation (hc/accounts/forms.py:168-172) and reach TokenBucket.authorize_totp_code at hc/accounts/views.py:891 with the same user and code, entering authorize at hc/api/models.py:1143 with capacity 1 (hc/api/models.py:1253-1259). When no totpc row exists, both sides' get_or_create at hc/api/models.py:1145 read before either writes (the loser's INSERT fails on the unique constraint at hc/api/models.py:1138 and re-reads tokens=1.0), so both compute 1.0-1.0>=0 at hc/api/models.py:1152-1153 and both save and return True at hc/api/models.py:1160-1163, logging in twice at hc/accounts/views.py:894-896. The same lost update occurs if the row already holds tokens=1.0: SELECT, SELECT, UPDATE, UPDATE, which read-committed permits since the SELECTs take no locks (the code itself notes the overwrite at hc/api/models.py:1157-1159, fatal here because single-use is the security property per hc/api/models.py:1256-1258). The switch window spans whole DB round-trips that release the GIL, and separate workers share no GIL at all, so CPython with the GIL can interleave here.
